subject: POC readiness, success criteria, and current blockers — VentureTech
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@venturetech.ai>, John Smyth <john.smyth@venturetech.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC readiness, success criteria, and current blockers — VentureTech

Hi Alice / John —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned before the POC kickoff: 

POC scope (agreed on call):
- Inference integration for VentureTech’s document-search feature using Redwood hosted API (model: rwd-3b-opt).
- Evaluate throughput and latency at peak query volumes (~50 qps).
- Validate embedding accuracy on the 10k test corpus you shared.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) 95th percentile latency <= 150 ms for single-turn queries under test harness.
2) Embedding cosine recall >= 0.88 on provided eval set.
3) No PII leakage on sampled outputs (pass SOC-scope checks).
4) End-to-end integration documented and reproducible by your infra team.

Timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): NDA + procurement kickoff; access for test data (Alice) + sample schema.
- Week 1: Redwood delivers POC checklist, baseline run, and test harness.
- Week 2: Joint runs, collect metrics, and tune batching/quantization.
- Week 3: Final report + decision meeting.

Owners:
- VentureTech: Alice (technical lead), John (procurement/contract).
- Redwood: Lauren (engagement owner), Rishi (technical lead), Stephanie (solutions + success).

Immediate asks for today:
1) Alice — confirm who will provision S3 test bucket and what credentials format you prefer.
2) John / procurement — confirm PO cadence or if we should proceed on a pilot MSA + T&Cs.
3) Confirm acceptance of the success criteria above (or flag any additions).

Attachments: I’ve attached a concise POC checklist, the sample schema you referenced, and a live risk log (we’ll update this).

I’ll also log expected blockers up front so we can triage them quickly: authentication/credentials, sample schema mismatches (tokenization), and data residency rules.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment stubs: redwood_poc-checklist.pdf (7 pages), vt_sample-schema.json (snippet), poc-risk-log.xlsx
From: Alice Park <alice.park@venturetech.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smyth <john.smyth@venturetech.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness, success criteria, and current blockers — VentureTech

Thanks Lauren — this is helpful. Quick answers/notes: 

- We’ll create an S3 bucket and share a short-term service principal key with your team. I’ll confirm the exact ARN by EOD Monday.
- Procurement: John, can you confirm whether we should sign the pilot MSA or route through our standard vendor onboarding?
- Success criteria: the latency target looks fine; for embeddings we’d prefer recall >= 0.90 for our top-10 retrievals if that’s reasonable.
- Data residency: some of the dataset originates in EU. We need to ensure logs and any persisted artifacts stay in the US-only environment during the pilot. Please confirm.

One risk I want flagged: our dataset includes scanned PDFs with OCR artifacts — tokenization differences could produce noise. Can Redwood advise on tokenization and token-embedding parity?

I’ll loop in procurement as soon as John confirms.

Best,
Alice
Senior Product Manager, VentureTech Analytics
alice.park@venturetech.ai
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@venturetech.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: POC readiness — operational items + risk assignments

Team — forwarding Alice’s note. I’ve pulled together immediate mitigation steps we should own and who to escalate to if we hit blockers. Please review and add timelines: 

1) Credentials + bucket access (owner: Stephanie) — Stephanie to validate auth formats we can accept and prepare upload checklist for VentureTech.
2) Tokenization / OCR noise (owner: Rishi) — run small parity test on the sample schema Alice sent; propose normalization pipeline and embed compare.
3) Data residency constraint (owner: Lauren) — confirm Redwood can run pilot in US-only hosting for logs and artifacts; raise with infra if not possible.
4) Procurement path (owner: Lauren) — coordinate with John / legal; propose pilot MSA + invoice.

Escalation path: 
- If we hit a >24h blocker on dataset ingestion or tokenization parity, escalate to Chloe Martin (technical director) for priority engineering triage.
- For SLA/contract exceptions, escalate to Finance + Legal (cc chain will be provided).

Please add estimated completion dates inline and I’ll send a consolidated plan back to VentureTech.

— Lauren

Onward: Stephanie, please share the auth checklist by COB tomorrow; Rishi — can you run the tokenization sample by tomorrow as well?
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@venturetech.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness — tokenization parity test results (initial)

Lauren / team / Alice —

I ran a quick parity check against the vt_sample-schema.json Alice attached. Summary:
- Found a tokenization drift on scanned PDF content (OCR punctuation and ligatures). Our tokenizer produced different split points for ~6% of tokens in the sample (affects rare proper nouns).
- Impact on embedding similarity: top-10 recall drop from 0.91 -> 0.84 in the initial run (with current preprocessing).

Proposed mitigations (short term):
1) Normalization pre-step: unicode normalization + ligature mapping + whitespace collapse (low effort).
2) Fuzzy-match layer in retrieval: allow edit-distance window on query normalization for scanned content.
3) For the POC only, run a warmed KV-cache on normalized tokens to reduce variance during metric collection.

If we implement (1) + (3) we should recover recall to ~0.89–0.90. Full fix (OCR-specific token mapper) is a medium priority engineering task (ETA 3–4 weeks).

Blocker assessment: not blocking kickoff. But if VentureTech requires immediate 0.90+ recall without tolerance, we need engineering hours or to narrow the eval to non-scanned docs.

Escalation: If normalization patch introduces perf regressions, Chloe — please prioritize kernel/embedding tuning (cc’d).

I’ll push a branch with the normalization script and a test harness link to the drive.

— Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: John Smyth <john.smyth@venturetech.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alice Park <alice.park@venturetech.ai>
Cc: procurement@venturetech.ai, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness, success criteria, and current blockers — VentureTech

Lauren / team —

Procurement is OK to proceed on a pilot MSA. We’ll aim to have a signed pilot agreement by end of week (internal approvals permitting). Please proceed with the technical kickoff.

On the technical side, appreciate Rishi’s note — the OCR issue is expected. For the pilot we accept the proposed mitigations and a target of 0.89–0.90 recall given the scanned content. If you can document that normalization step as part of the POC report that will suffice for our decisioning.

I’ll share the PO path and a short vendor form this afternoon. Also: Alice will upload a sanitized sample dataset to the S3 bucket by tomorrow noon. Link will be sent.

Thanks,
John Smyth
Head of Procurement, VentureTech Analytics
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-07T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC readiness, success criteria, and current blockers — VentureTech (consolidated plan)

Hi all —

Consolidated plan and owners (finalized):
- Credentials & bucket: Stephanie — checklist uploaded to drive (link above). ETA: 2026-10-08T12:00Z.
- Tokenization normalization + test harness: Rishi — branch + instructions in Drive, baseline run by 2026-10-08T18:00Z.
- Pilot hosting & logs: Lauren — confirmed US-only storage for POC artifacts; infra will ensure no EU logs are persisted.
- Reporting & decision meeting: Lauren & Stephanie — deliverable by 2026-10-15; meeting to review results scheduled for 2026-10-16.

Risk log (high-level items we’ll track in poc-risk-log.xlsx):
- OCR token drift (medium) — mitigation: normalization script + fuzzy retrieval; escalation: Chloe if metric regressions persist.
- Credentials delay (low) — mitigation: temporary signed upload token; owner: Stephanie.
- Data residency question (low) — mitigation: US-only pilot; owner: Lauren.

Next steps for VentureTech:
1) Upload sanitized sample dataset to S3 and share access.
2) Confirm PO/pilot MSA path (John).
3) Accept the slightly relaxed recall threshold for scanned docs (0.89–0.90) for this pilot.

I’ll attach the POC checklist and the current risk log to the HubSpot deal and keep the Drive folder updated. If anything changes, flag immediately and we’ll escalate per the path above.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to kickoff.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_poc-checklist.pdf, poc-risk-log.xlsx
